hook: This capsule had just come home from a trip to the Moon.
narration: This capsule had just come home from a trip to the Moon.
NASA's Orion splashed down in the Pacific on December 11, 2022, after twenty-five and a half days away.
No one was aboard. Artemis One was the test flight before astronauts ride it.
Parachutes slowed it down for the last stretch to the water.
Coming back from the Moon, a capsule hits the air far faster than one returning from the space station, so its heat shield takes a much harder beating.
The orange bags on top are airbags that flip the capsule upright if it lands upside down.
Navy boats raced out to it from the USS Portland.
outcome: Divers hooked up Orion, and the recovery team towed it back to the USS Portland.
title: Orion splashes down after the Moon
question_comment: Would you ride the next one around the Moon?

facts.claim: Orion splashed down in the Pacific Dec 11 2022 after a 25.5 day Moon mission
facts.source_quote: At 12:40 p.m. EST, Dec. 11, 2022, NASA’s Orion spacecraft for the Artemis I mission splashed down in the Pacific Ocean after a 25.5 day mission to the Moon.

facts.claim: Recovered by NASA and Navy teams aboard USS Portland
facts.source_quote: Orion will be recovered by NASA’s Landing and Recovery team, U.S. Navy and Department of Defense partners aboard the USS Portland.

description:
NASA's Orion spacecraft splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on Dec. 11, 2022, after the 25.5 day Artemis I mission to the Moon, and was recovered by NASA and U.S. Navy teams aboard the USS Portland. No one was aboard.
